newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram concerned over infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram concerned over infrastructure.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Thursday expressed serious concern over sluggish growth in key infrastructure areas, the Press Trust of India said.
"I intend to place this matter before the cabinet committee on infrastructure so that the ministries concerned can pay attention to these sectors," the news agency quoted Chidambaram as saying.

He said 6.8 percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 1996/97 (April-March) was cause for satisfaction, but not for celebration. GDP growth would have crossed seven percent if the infrastructure sector had expanded more rapidly, the minister said.
In 1996/97, the electricity, gas and water supply sector, representing key infrastructure areas, grew by just 3.8 percent compared to 9.1 percent in the previous year, when GDP grew by 7.1 percent.

Government estimates show India needs investment worth $30 billion in roads over the next five years, between $15 billion and $20 billion to upgrade port infrastructure and $80 billion in the power sector by the year 2002 to meet current demand projections.
